title: The Sunday Read: 'The Woman Who Might Find Us Another Earth'

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》旗下的日报通讯《DealBook》负责商业和政策报道。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、佐兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Hi, my name is Chris Jones, and I'm a writer based in Port Hope, Ontario, Canada.
sentences.zh: 你好，我叫克里斯·琼斯，是一名居住在加拿大安大略省霍普港的作家。

sentences.en: Like you, I've spent a lot of time inside my house, even more than normal for a writer, over the past several weeks.
sentences.zh: 和你们一样，过去几周里，我大部分时间都待在家里，甚至比我平时作为作家待在家里的时间还要长。

sentences.en: I'd like to introduce you to someone named Sarah Seeger, who I think might help you get through this, get through this pretty difficult time for all of us.
sentences.zh: 我想向大家介绍一位叫萨拉·西格的人，我认为她或许能帮助大家度过这段对我们所有人来说都相当困难的时期。

sentences.en: She's someone who endured and survived terrible personal loss, but is also doing groundbreaking, important, really inspiring work.
sentences.zh: 她曾经历并幸免于巨大的个人损失，但同时也在从事着开创性的、重要的、真正鼓舞人心的工作。

sentences.en: She is an astrophysicist who is searching for other life in the universe, and she believes that she will be the one to find it.
sentences.zh: 她是一位天体物理学家，正在寻找宇宙中的其他生命，并且她相信自己会是那个发现它们的人。

sentences.en: She wants to be able to take her kids outside and point to one star and go, the planet next to that star has someone looking back at you on it.
sentences.zh: 她希望有一天能带着孩子走到户外，指着一颗星星说，那颗星星旁边的行星上，有人正在回望着你们。

sentences.en: So in the middle of this quarantine, I've been going outside every night and looking at the sky in a totally different way because of the time I spent with Sarah.
sentences.zh: 所以，在这次隔离期间，因为我和萨拉相处的那段时间，我每天晚上都会走到户外，以一种完全不同的方式仰望天空。

sentences.en: And I think we could all use at this moment a little perspective, a little hope, and maybe
sentences.zh: 我认为此时此刻我们都需要一点视角，一点希望，或许

sentences.en: in some strange way, Sarah's work and the stars might give you just a little bit of light at the end of the tunnel.
sentences.zh: 以某种奇妙的方式，萨拉的工作和那些星星能为你带来隧道尽头的一丝微光。

sentences.en: So here's my story, The Woman Who Might Find Us Another Earth, read by Gabber
sentences.zh: 这就是我的故事，《可能为我们找到另一个地球的女人》，由加伯·

sentences.en: Zachman.
sentences.zh: 扎克曼朗读。

sentences.en: Like many astrophysicists, Sarah Seeger sometimes has a problem with her perception of scale.
sentences.zh: 像许多天体物理学家一样，萨拉·西格有时会对尺度的感知感到困惑。

sentences.en: Knowing that there are hundreds of billions of galaxies, and that each might contain hundreds
sentences.zh: 知道有数千亿个星系，而每个星系可能包含数

sentences.en: of billions of stars, can make the lives of astrophysicists and even those closest to them seem insignificant.
sentences.zh: 千亿颗恒星，这会让天体物理学家甚至他们最亲近的人的生活显得微不足道。

sentences.en: Their work can also, paradoxically, bolster their sense of themselves.
sentences.zh: 但矛盾的是，他们的工作也能增强他们的自我意识。

sentences.en: Believing that you alone might answer the question, are we alone, requires considerable ego.
sentences.zh: 相信只有自己能回答“我们是否孤独”这个问题，需要相当大的自我。

sentences.en: Astrophysicists are forever toggling between feelings of bigness and smallness, of hubris and humility, depending on whether they're looking out or within.
sentences.zh: 天体物理学家总是在宏大与渺小、傲慢与谦卑的感觉之间摇摆，这取决于他们是在向外看还是向内看。

sentences.en: One perfect blue sky fall day,
sentences.zh: 在一个完美的秋日蓝天之下，

sentences.en: Seeger boarded a train in Concord, Massachusetts on her way to her office at MIT and realized she didn't have her phone.
sentences.zh: 西格在马萨诸塞州康科德登上了一列前往麻省理工学院办公室的火车，才意识到自己没带手机。

sentences.en: She couldn't seem to decide whether this was or wasn't a big deal.
sentences.zh: 她似乎无法决定这到底算不算一件大事。

sentences.en: Not having her phone would make the day tricky in some ways, because her sons, 13-year-old Max and 11-year-old
sentences.zh: 没带手机会让这一天变得有些棘手，因为她13岁的儿子马克斯和11岁的

sentences.en: Alex, had a soccer game after school, and she would need to coordinate a ride to watch them.
sentences.zh: 亚历克斯放学后有一场足球比赛，她需要协调搭车去观看。

sentences.en: She also wanted to be able to find and sit with her best friend, Melissa, who sometimes takes the same train to work.
sentences.zh: 她还想找到她最好的朋友梅丽莎并和她坐在一起，梅丽莎有时会坐同一班火车上班。

sentences.en: She's my best friend, but I know she has other best friends, Seeger said, wanting to make the nature of their relationship clear.
sentences.zh: “她是我最好的朋友，但我知道她还有其他最好的朋友，”西格说，她想明确她们关系的性质。

sentences.en: She is an admirer of clarity.
sentences.zh: 她是一个崇尚清晰的人。

sentences.en: She also likes absolutes, wide open spaces, and time to think, but not too much time to think.
sentences.zh: 她也喜欢绝对、广阔的空间和思考的时间，但思考的时间不能太多。

sentences.en: She took out her laptop to see if she could email Melissa.
sentences.zh: 她拿出笔记本电脑，想看看能不能给梅丽莎发邮件。

sentences.en: The train's Wi-Fi was down.
sentences.zh: 火车的Wi-Fi坏了。

sentences.en: She would have to occupy herself on the commute alone.
sentences.zh: 她只能在通勤路上独自打发时间。

sentences.en: Seeger's office is on the 17th floor of MIT's Green Building, the tallest building in Cambridge.
sentences.zh: 西格的办公室位于麻省理工学院格林大楼的17楼，这是剑桥市最高的建筑。

sentences.en: It's roof dotted with meteorological and radar equipment.
sentences.zh: 楼顶上布满了气象和雷达设备。

sentences.en: She is a tenured professor of physics and of planetary science, certified a genius by the MacArthur Foundation in 2013.
sentences.zh: 她是物理学和行星科学的终身教授，2013年被麦克阿瑟基金会认证为天才。

sentences.en: Her area of expertise is the relatively new field of exoplanets, planets that orbit stars other than our sun.
sentences.zh: 她的专业领域是相对较新的系外行星领域，即围绕太阳以外的恒星运行的行星。

sentences.en: More particular, she wants to find an Earth-like exoplanet, a rocky planet of reasonable mass that
sentences.zh: 更具体地说，她想找到一颗类地系外行星，一颗质量适中、岩石构成的行星，

sentences.en: orbits its star within a temperate, Goldilocks zone that is not too hot or too cold, which would allow water to remain liquid, and determine that there is life on it.
sentences.zh: 它在其恒星的温和“金发姑娘区”内运行，既不太热也不太冷，这使得水能够保持液态，并确定上面存在生命。

sentences.en: That is as simple as her math gets.
sentences.zh: 这就是她数学中最简单的部分。

sentences.en: Her office is spare.
sentences.zh: 她的办公室很简朴。

sentences.en: There is a set of bookshelves, optics, and Asteroids 3 and How to Build a Habitable
sentences.zh: 有一排书架，上面放着《光学》、《小行星3》和《如何建造一颗宜居的

sentences.en: Planet, topped with a row of certificates and honors leaning against a chalkboard covered with equations.
sentences.zh: 行星》，顶部是一排靠在写满方程式的黑板上的证书和奖项。

sentences.en: In addition to the MacArthur Award, which doesn't come with a certificate but with $625,000, she is proudest of her election to the National Academy of Sciences.
sentences.zh: 除了麦克阿瑟奖（没有证书，但有62.5万美元奖金），她最引以为豪的是当选美国国家科学院院士。

sentences.en: Although the line between lunacy and scientific fact is constantly shifting, the search for aliens still occupies the shadows of cranks,
sentences.zh: 尽管疯狂与科学事实之间的界限在不断变化，但寻找外星人仍然占据着怪人的阴影地带，

sentences.en: and Seeger hears from them almost daily, or at least her assistant does.
sentences.zh: 西格几乎每天都能收到他们的来信，或者至少她的助理会收到。

sentences.en: By the standards of her universe, Seeger is famous.
sentences.zh: 按照她所在领域的标准，西格很有名。

sentences.en: She is careful about the company she keeps and the words she chooses.
sentences.zh: 她对自己的社交圈和言辞非常谨慎。

sentences.en: She isn't searching for aliens.
sentences.zh: 她不是在寻找外星人。

sentences.en: She's searching for exoplanets that show signs of life.
sentences.zh: 她是在寻找显示生命迹象的系外行星。

sentences.en: She's searching for a familiar blue dot in the sky.
sentences.zh: 她是在寻找天空中那个熟悉的蓝色圆点。

sentences.en: That means Seeger, who is 45, has given herself a very difficult problem to solve, the problem that has always plagued astronomy, which, at its essence, is the study of light.
sentences.zh: 这意味着45岁的西格给自己出了一个非常难解的难题，这个问题一直困扰着天文学，而天文学本质上就是对光的研究。

sentences.en: Light wages war with itself.
sentences.zh: 光与自身交战。

sentences.en: Light pollutes.
sentences.zh: 光造成污染。

sentences.en: Light blinds.
sentences.zh: 光令人目盲。

sentences.en: Seeger has a commanding view of downtown Boston from her office window.
sentences.zh: 从办公室窗户望去，西格可以将波士顿市中心尽收眼底。

sentences.en: She can sweep her eyes, hazel, and in tents, all the way from the gold Capitol Dome to Fenway Park.
sentences.zh: 她那双淡褐色、专注的眼睛可以扫视从金色的议会大厦圆顶到芬威球场的整个区域。

sentences.en: When Seeger works at night and the Red Sox are in town, she sometimes has to close her curtains, because the ballpark's white lights are so glaring.
sentences.zh: 当西格在晚上工作而红袜队在主场比赛时，她有时不得不拉上窗帘，因为球场的白光太刺眼了。

sentences.en: And on this morning, after the sun completed its rise, her enviable vista became unbearable.
sentences.zh: 而在这一天早上，太阳升起之后，她那令人羡慕的视野变得难以忍受。

sentences.en: It was searing, and she had to draw her curtains.
sentences.zh: 阳光灼人，她不得不拉上窗帘。

sentences.en: That's how light can be the object of her passion and also her enemy.
sentences.zh: 这就是光，它既是她热情的对象，也是她的敌人。

sentences.en: Little lights, exoplanets, are washed out by bigger lights, their stars, the way stars are washed out by our biggest light, the sun.
sentences.zh: 微小的光——系外行星，被更大的光——它们的恒星所淹没，就像星星被我们最大的光——太阳所淹没一样。

sentences.en: Seeger's challenge is that she has dedicated her life to the search for the smallest lights.
sentences.zh: 西格面临的挑战是，她毕生致力于寻找这些微小的光。

sentences.en: The vastness of space almost defies conventional measures of distance.
sentences.zh: 太空的广袤几乎挑战了传统的距离衡量标准。

sentences.en: Driving the speed limit to Alpha Centauri, the nearest star grouping to the sun would take 50 million years or so.
sentences.zh: 以限速驾驶前往距离太阳最近的恒星群——半人马座阿尔法星，大约需要5000万年。

sentences.en: Our fastest current spacecraft would make the trip in a relatively brisk 73,000 years.
sentences.zh: 我们目前最快的航天器完成这段旅程也需要相对较快的7.3万年。

sentences.en: The next nearest star is six light years away.
sentences.zh: 最近的下一颗恒星距离我们六光年。

sentences.en: To rocket across our galaxy would take about 23,000 times as long as a trip to Alpha Centauri, or 1.7 billion years.
sentences.zh: 要穿越我们的银河系，所需时间大约是前往半人马座阿尔法星的2.3万倍，即17亿年。

sentences.en: And the Milky Way is just one of hundreds of billions of galaxies.
sentences.zh: 而银河系只是数千亿个星系中的一个。

sentences.en: The Hubble Space Telescope once searched a tiny fragment of the night sky, the size of a penny held at arm's length, that was long thought by astronomers to be dark.
sentences.zh: 哈勃太空望远镜曾经搜索过夜空中一小片区域，大小相当于手臂伸直时的一枚硬币，天文学家长期以来一直认为那里是黑暗的。

sentences.en: It contained 3,000 previously unseen points of light.
sentences.zh: 结果它包含了3000个以前未见的光点。

sentences.en: Not 3,000 new stars.
sentences.zh: 不是3000颗新恒星。

sentences.en: 3,000 new galaxies.
sentences.zh: 而是3000个新星系。

sentences.en: And in all those galaxies, orbiting around some large percentage of each of their virtually countless stars.
sentences.zh: 而在所有这些星系中，围绕着它们几乎数不清的恒星中很大一部分运行着。

sentences.en: Planets.
sentences.zh: 行星。

sentences.en: Planets like Neptune.
sentences.zh: 像海王星那样的行星。

sentences.en: Planets like Mercury.
sentences.zh: 像水星那样的行星。

sentences.en: Planets like Earth.
sentences.zh: 像地球那样的行星。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果可以免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: As late as the 1990s, exoplanets remained a largely theoretical construct.
sentences.zh: 直到20世纪90年代，系外行星在很大程度上仍然是一个理论构想。

sentences.en: Logic dictated that they must be out there, but proof of their existence remained as out of reach as they were.
sentences.zh: 逻辑上推断它们一定存在，但证明它们存在的证据却和它们本身一样遥不可及。

sentences.en: Some scientists dismissed efforts to find exoplanets as stamp collecting, a derogatory term within the community for hunting new, unreachable lights just to name them.
sentences.zh: 一些科学家对寻找系外行星的努力不屑一顾，称之为“集邮”，这是该领域内的一个贬义词，指为了命名而寻找新的、无法触及的光点。

sentences.en: Even among astronomers, there can be too much stargazing.
sentences.zh: 即使在天文学家中间，也可能存在过多的“观星”。

sentences.en: It wasn't until 1995 that the colossal 51 Pegasi b, the first widely recognized exoplanet orbiting a sun-like star,
sentences.zh: 直到1995年，巨大的飞马座51b，第一颗被广泛认可的围绕类太阳恒星运行的系外行星，

sentences.en: was found by a pair of Swiss astronomers using a light-analyzing spectrograph.
sentences.zh: 才被两位瑞士天文学家使用光分析光谱仪发现。

sentences.en: The Swiss didn't see 51 Pegasi b.
sentences.zh: 瑞士人并没有直接看到飞马座51b。

sentences.en: No one has.
sentences.zh: 没有人看到过。

sentences.en: By using a complex mathematical method called radial velocity, they witnessed the planet's gravitational effect on its star and deduced that it must be there.
sentences.zh: 通过使用一种称为径向速度的复杂数学方法，他们观察到了行星对其恒星的引力影响，并推断它一定存在。

sentences.en: There has been an explosion of knowledge in the relatively short time since,
sentences.zh: 此后相对较短的时间内，知识出现了爆炸式增长，

sentences.en: in part because of Seeger's pioneering theoretical work in using light to study the composition of alien atmospheres.
sentences.zh: 部分归功于西格在利用光研究外星大气成分方面的开创性理论工作。

sentences.en: When starlight passes through a planet's atmosphere, certain potentially life-betraying gases, like oxygen, will block particular wavelengths of light.
sentences.zh: 当星光穿过行星大气层时，某些可能泄露生命信息的特定气体（如氧气）会阻挡特定波长的光。

sentences.en: It's a way of seeing something by looking for what's not there.
sentences.zh: 这是一种通过寻找“不存在的东西”来观察事物的方法。

sentences.en: Light, or its absence, is also the root of something called the transit technique, a newer, more efficient way than radial velocity of finding exoplanets by looking at their stars.
sentences.zh: 光，或者它的缺失，也是所谓的“凌日法”的根源，这是一种比径向速度法更新、更有效的通过观察恒星来寻找系外行星的方法。

sentences.en: It treats light almost like music, something that can be sensed more accurately than it can be seen.
sentences.zh: 它几乎把光当作音乐来对待，一种比视觉更能被精确感知的东西。

sentences.en: The Kepler Space Telescope, launched in 2009 and now trailing 75 million miles behind Earth, detects exoplanets when they orbit between their stars and the telescope's mirrors,
sentences.zh: 开普勒太空望远镜于2009年发射，目前在地球后方7500万英里处运行，当系外行星运行到其恒星和望远镜的镜片之间时，它能探测到系外行星，

sentences.en: making tiny but measurable partial eclipses.
sentences.zh: 造成微小但可测量的部分日食。

sentences.en: A planet the size of Jupiter passing in front of its sun might result in a 1% dip in the amount of starlight Kepler receives,
sentences.zh: 一颗木星大小的行星在其太阳前方经过，可能会导致开普勒接收到的星光减少1%，

sentences.en: a drop that in time reveals itself to be as regular as rhythm, as an orbit.
sentences.zh: 这种下降随着时间的推移，显现出像节奏、像轨道一样规律。

sentences.en: The transit technique has led to a bonanza of finds.
sentences.zh: 凌日法带来了大量的发现。

sentences.en: In May, NASA announced the validation of 1,284 exoplanets, by far the largest single collection of new worlds yet.
sentences.zh: 5月，美国国家航空航天局（NASA）宣布验证了1284颗系外行星，这是迄今为止最大规模的新世界集合。

sentences.en: There are now 3,414 confirmed exoplanets and an additional 4,696 suspected ones, the count forever increasing.
sentences.zh: 目前已有3414颗确认的系外行星，另有4696颗疑似行星，数量还在不断增加。

sentences.en: Before Kepler, the nature of the transit technique meant that most of those exoplanets were hot Jupiters,
sentences.zh: 在开普勒之前，凌日法的性质意味着大多数系外行星都是“热木星”，

sentences.en: giant balls of hydrogen and helium with short orbits, making them scalding, lifeless behemoths.
sentences.zh: 它们是巨大的氢和氦球体，轨道很短，这使它们成为灼热、毫无生机的庞然大物。

sentences.en: But in April 2014, Kepler found its first Earth-sized exoplanet in its star's habitable zone,
sentences.zh: 但在2014年4月，开普勒在其恒星的宜居带内发现了第一颗地球大小的系外行星，

sentences.en: Kepler-186f.
sentences.zh: 开普勒-186f。

sentences.en: It's about 10% larger than Earth and orbits on the outer reaches of where the temperature could allow life.
sentences.zh: 它比地球大10%左右，运行在温度可能允许生命存在的轨道外缘。

sentences.en: No one knows the mass, composition, or density of Kepler-186f, but its discovery remains a revelation.
sentences.zh: 没有人知道开普勒-186f的质量、成分或密度，但它的发现仍然是一个启示。

sentences.en: Kepler was searching, somewhat blindly, an impossibly small sliver of space.
sentences.zh: 开普勒当时是在盲目地搜索一小片极其狭窄的太空。

sentences.en: And it found a potentially habitable world more quickly than anyone might have guessed.
sentences.zh: 它比任何人预想的都要快地发现了一个潜在的宜居世界。

sentences.en: In August, astronomers at the European Southern Observatory announced that they had detected
sentences.zh: 8月，欧洲南方天文台的天文学家宣布，他们探测到了

sentences.en: a somewhat similar planet orbiting Proxima Centauri, the single star closest to us after the Sun.
sentences.zh: 一颗围绕比邻星运行的类似行星，比邻星是除太阳外距离我们最近的单星。

sentences.en: They named it Proxima Centauri b.
sentences.zh: 他们将其命名为比邻星b。

sentences.en: Studying the data, Seeger supported the discovery and agreed that it might boast a life-sustaining, or at least non-life-threatening, surface temperature.
sentences.zh: 研究数据后，西格支持这一发现，并同意它可能拥有维持生命，或者至少是不威胁生命的表面温度。

sentences.en: There are now nearly 300 confirmed exoplanets or candidates orbiting within the habitable zones of their stars.
sentences.zh: 目前已有近300颗确认的或候选的系外行星在其恒星的宜居带内运行。

sentences.en: Extrapolating the math, NASA scientists now believe that there are tens of billions of potentially life-sustaining planets in the Milky Way alone.
sentences.zh: 推算这些数学数据，NASA的科学家现在认为，仅在银河系中就有数百亿颗潜在的维持生命的行星。

sentences.en: The odds practically guarantee that a habitable planet is somewhere out there, and that someone, or something else, is too.
sentences.zh: 概率几乎保证了宜居行星就在那里，而且某个人，或者某种其他东西，也就在那里。

sentences.en: In some ways, the search for life is now where the search for exoplanets was 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，寻找生命现在处于20年前寻找系外行星的阶段。

sentences.en: Common sense suggests a presence that we can't confirm.
sentences.zh: 常识暗示了一种我们无法证实的存在。

sentences.en: Seeger understands that we won't know they're out there until we more truly lay eyes on their home and see something that reminds us of ours.
sentences.zh: 西格明白，除非我们更真实地注视它们的家园，看到一些让我们想起我们自己的东西，否则我们不会知道它们就在那里。

sentences.en: Maybe it's the color blue.
sentences.zh: 也许是蓝色。

sentences.en: Maybe it's clouds.
sentences.zh: 也许是云。

sentences.en: Maybe, however many generations from now, it's the orange electrical grids of alien cities, the black rectangles of their lightless central parks.
sentences.zh: 也许，无论多少代人之后，那是外星城市橙色的电网，是它们无光中央公园的黑色矩形。

sentences.en: But how could we ever begin to look that far?
sentences.zh: 但我们怎么可能开始看得那么远呢？

sentences.en: Everything brave has to start somewhere, Seeger says.
sentences.zh: “所有勇敢的事情都必须从某个地方开始，”西格说。

sentences.en: The beginning of her next potential breakthrough hangs on the wall opposite the window in her office.
sentences.zh: 她下一个潜在突破的开端挂在她办公室窗户对面的墙上。

sentences.en: It is a two-thirds-scale model of a single petal of something called the starshade.
sentences.zh: 这是一个名为“星影”装置的单片花瓣的三分之二比例模型。

sentences.en: She has been a leading proponent of the starshade project, and outside her teaching, it is one of her principal professional concerns.
sentences.zh: 她是星影项目的主要倡导者，除了教学之外，这是她主要的专业关注点之一。

sentences.en: Imagine that far-off aliens with our present technology were trying to find us.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，遥远的外星人如果拥有我们现在的技术，试图找到我们。

sentences.en: At best, they would see Jupiter.
sentences.zh: 充其量，他们只能看到木星。

sentences.en: We would be lost in the sun's glare.
sentences.zh: 我们会迷失在太阳的强光中。

sentences.en: The same is true for our trying to see them.
sentences.zh: 我们试图看到他们时也是如此。

sentences.en: The starshade is a way to block the light from our theoretical twin sun, an idea floated in 1962 by Lyman Spitzer, who also laid the groundwork for space telescopes like Hubble.
sentences.zh: 星影是一种阻挡我们理论上的双子太阳光线的方法，这个想法由莱曼·斯皮策在1962年提出，他也为哈勃等太空望远镜奠定了基础。

sentences.en: The starshade is a huge shield, about 100 feet across.
sentences.zh: 星影是一个巨大的盾牌，直径约100英尺。

sentences.en: For practical reasons that have to do with the bending of light, but also lend it a certain cosmic beauty, the starshade is shaped exactly like a sunflower.
sentences.zh: 出于与光线弯曲有关的实际原因，但也赋予了它某种宇宙之美，星影的形状完全像一朵向日葵。

sentences.en: By Seeger's hopeful reckoning, one day the starshade will be rocketed into space and unfurled, working in tandem with a new space telescope like the WFIRST,
sentences.zh: 按照西格充满希望的推算，有一天星影将被发射到太空并展开，与像WFIRST这样的新型太空望远镜协同工作，

sentences.en: scheduled to launch in the mid-2020s.
sentences.zh: 计划于2020年代中期发射。

sentences.en: When the telescope is aimed at a particular planetary system, lasers will help align the starshade, floating more than 18,000 miles away,
sentences.zh: 当望远镜对准某个特定的行星系统时，激光将帮助校准远在 18000 英里之外的星影仪，

sentences.en: between the telescope and the distant star, closing the curtains on it.
sentences.zh: 置于望远镜与遥远的恒星之间，遮挡住恒星的光芒。

sentences.en: With the big light extinguished, the little lights, including a potential Earth-like planet and everything it might represent, will become clear.
sentences.zh: 随着强光被遮蔽，微弱的光芒——包括一颗潜在的类地行星及其所代表的一切——将变得清晰可见。

sentences.en: We will see them.
sentences.zh: 我们将看到它们。

sentences.en: The trouble is that sometimes the simplest ideas are the most complicated to execute.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，有时最简单的想法执行起来却最为复杂。

sentences.en: About once a decade since Spitzer's proposal, he could work out the math but not the mechanics, someone else has taken up the cause,
sentences.zh: 自斯皮策提出这一构想以来，大约每十年就会有人接手这项事业，他们能算出数学原理却无法解决机械难题，

sentences.en: advancing the starshade slightly closer to reality before technological or political inertia set in.
sentences.zh: 在技术或政治惯性介入之前，将星影仪向现实推进了一小步。

sentences.en: Three years ago,
sentences.zh: 三年前，

sentences.en: Seeger joined a new NASA-sponsored study to try to overcome the final practical hurdles.
sentences.zh: 西格加入了一项由美国国家航空航天局（NASA）资助的新研究，试图克服最后的实际障碍。

sentences.en: NASA then chose her from among her fellow committee members to lead the effort.
sentences.zh: 随后，NASA 从委员会成员中选中她来领导这项工作。

sentences.en: After those decades of false starts,
sentences.zh: 在经历了数十年的无果而终后，

sentences.en: Seeger and her team have already succeeded in making the starshade seem like a real possibility.
sentences.zh: 西格和她的团队已经成功让星影仪看起来成为了一种真正的可能。

sentences.en: NASA recognized it as a technology project, which is astral bureaucracy-speak for this might actually happen.
sentences.zh: NASA 将其认定为一个技术项目，在航天官僚术语中，这意味着这事儿真的可能实现。

sentences.en: Today, the starshade is a piece of buildable, functional hardware.
sentences.zh: 如今，星影仪已是一件可制造、可运作的硬件设备。

sentences.en: Seeger packs that single petal into a battered black case and wheels it, along with a miniature model of the starshade, into classrooms and conferences and the halls of Congress,
sentences.zh: 西格将那片花瓣状的组件装进一个破旧的黑色箱子，连同星影仪的微缩模型一起，带进教室、会议厅和国会大厦，

sentences.en: trying to find the momentum and hundreds of millions of dollars that allow impossible things to exiSt.
sentences.zh: 试图寻找动力和数亿美元的资金，让不可能的事物成为现实。

sentences.en: If I want the starshade to succeed,
sentences.zh: “如果我想让星影仪成功，

sentences.en: I have to help mastermind it,
sentences.zh: 我就必须协助策划它，”

sentences.en: Seeger says.
sentences.zh: 西格说。

sentences.en: The world sees me as the one who will find another Earth.
sentences.zh: “世人视我为那个将要找到另一个地球的人。”

sentences.en: She has her intelligence and her credentials and her audience.
sentences.zh: 她拥有智慧、资历和听众。

sentences.en: She has her focus.
sentences.zh: 她拥有专注力。

sentences.en: But maybe more than anything else,
sentences.zh: 但或许最重要的是，

sentences.en: Seeger understands in ways few of us do that sometimes you need darkness to see.
sentences.zh: 西格比我们大多数人更深刻地理解，有时你需要黑暗才能看见。

sentences.en: Seeger grew up in Toronto, wired in a way all her own.
sentences.zh: 西格在多伦多长大，她的思维方式独树一帜。

sentences.en: Ever since I was a child, there was just something about me that wasn't quite like the others, she says.
sentences.zh: “从小到大，我身上总有些地方和别人不太一样，”她说。

sentences.en: Kids know how to sort through who's the same and who's different.
sentences.zh: 孩子们很擅长分辨谁是同类，谁是异类。

sentences.en: After her parents divorced, her father, Dr. David Seeger, achieved a certain fame by becoming one of the world's leaders in hair transplants.
sentences.zh: 父母离婚后，她的父亲大卫·西格博士因成为世界植发领域的领军人物之一而声名鹊起。

sentences.en: The Seeger Hair Transplant Center still operates and bears his name a decade after his death.
sentences.zh: 西格植发中心在他去世十年后仍在运营，并沿用着他的名字。

sentences.en: David Seeger was besotted with his bright daughter and wanted her to become a physician.
sentences.zh: 大卫·西格对聪慧的女儿宠爱有加，希望她能成为一名医生。

sentences.en: Seeger did her best to fit in.
sentences.zh: 西格尽了最大努力去融入群体。

sentences.en: Sometimes she did.
sentences.zh: 有时她做到了。

sentences.en: Mostly she didn't.
sentences.zh: 但大多数时候没有。

sentences.en: Eventually she gave up trying.
sentences.zh: 最终她放弃了尝试。

sentences.en: She still talks breathlessly, without enough modulation, she has learned by listening to other people talk.
sentences.zh: 她说话依然语速很快，缺乏抑扬顿挫，这是她通过倾听他人谈话学来的。

sentences.en: She has never had the patience to invest in something like watching TV.
sentences.zh: 她从未有耐心投入到看电视之类的事情上。

sentences.en: Things just move too slowly, she says.
sentences.zh: “事情进展得太慢了，”她说。

sentences.en: It feels like a drag.
sentences.zh: “感觉像是一种拖累。”

sentences.en: She sleeps a lot, but that's just a concession to her biology.
sentences.zh: 她睡得很多，但这只是对生理机能的妥协。

sentences.en: She recognizes that she's a more efficient machine when she's rested.
sentences.zh: 她意识到，休息充足时，她是一台更高效的机器。

sentences.en: But if Seeger's apartness didn't make her insecure, it also made her feel as though the expectations of others didn't apply to her.
sentences.zh: 但如果说西格的疏离感没有让她感到自卑，那也让她觉得别人的期望并不适用于她。

sentences.en: I loved the stars, she says.
sentences.zh: “我热爱星空，”她说。

sentences.en: When she was 16, she bought a telescope.
sentences.zh: 16 岁时，她买了一台望远镜。

sentences.en: Friendless for most of her childhood,
sentences.zh: 童年时期大多没有朋友的她，

sentences.en: Seeger eventually forged her way to her own vision of the good life.
sentences.zh: 最终开辟出了一条属于自己的美好生活之路。

sentences.en: She found and married a quiet man named Mike Weverick, whom she met on a ski trip with her canoe club.
sentences.zh: 她遇到了一个安静的男人迈克·韦弗里克并与他结婚，他们是在一次独木舟俱乐部的滑雪旅行中相识的。

sentences.en: He had seen something in her that nobody other than her father fully saw.
sentences.zh: 他在她身上看到了除她父亲之外无人能完全察觉的东西。

sentences.en: He saw her as special, as well as strange.
sentences.zh: 他视她为特别，也视她为怪异。

sentences.en: Later she graduated from Harvard, an early expert in exoplanets.
sentences.zh: 后来她从哈佛大学毕业，成为系外行星领域的早期专家。

sentences.en: 51 Pegasi B was discovered just when she was searching for a thesis topic.
sentences.zh: 飞马座 51b 正是在她寻找论文课题时被发现的。

sentences.en: I was born at the perfect time, she says.
sentences.zh: “我生逢其时，”她说。

sentences.en: She and Weverick had Max and Alex,
sentences.zh: 她和韦弗里克有了马克斯和亚历克斯，

sentences.en: Seeger was hired by MIT, and she and Weverick and the boys moved into a pretty yellow Victorian in Concord, Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 西格被麻省理工学院聘用，她和韦弗里克带着孩子们搬进了马萨诸塞州康科德市一栋漂亮的黄色维多利亚式住宅。

sentences.en: She took the train to work.
sentences.zh: 她乘火车上班。

sentences.en: Weverick, a freelance editor, managed just about everything that didn't involve the search for intelligent life in the universe.
sentences.zh: 韦弗里克是一名自由编辑，几乎打理着所有与寻找宇宙智慧生命无关的琐事。

sentences.en: Seeger never shopped for groceries, or cooked, or pumped gas.
sentences.zh: 西格从不去买菜、做饭或加油。

sentences.en: All she had to do was find another Earth.
sentences.zh: 她唯一要做的就是找到另一个地球。

sentences.en: Then, in the fall of 2009,
sentences.zh: 然而，在 2009 年秋天，

sentences.en: Weverick got a stomachache that drove him to bed.
sentences.zh: 韦弗里克胃痛难忍，卧床不起。

sentences.en: They figured it was the flu.
sentences.zh: 他们以为是流感。

sentences.en: Weverick didn't have the flu, but a rare cancer of the small intestine.
sentences.zh: 韦弗里克患的不是流感，而是一种罕见的小肠癌。

sentences.en: They were told that the initial prospects were good, and he fought the cancer sufferer's systematic fight.
sentences.zh: 他们被告知最初的预后良好，他像癌症患者一样进行了系统的抗争。

sentences.en: But while laws govern astrophysics, cancer is an anarchiSt.
sentences.zh: 但天体物理学有定律可循，癌症却是无政府主义者。

sentences.en: About a year after Weverick's diagnosis, he and Seeger went cross-country skiing, and he couldn't keep up.
sentences.zh: 在韦弗里克确诊约一年后，他和西格去越野滑雪，他已经跟不上了。

sentences.en: A few more terrible months passed, and he began writing out a methodical three-page list, practical advice for Seeger after his death.
sentences.zh: 又过了几个可怕的月头，他开始列出一份有条理的三页清单，那是他去世后留给西格的实用建议。

sentences.en: It wasn't a love letter.
sentences.zh: 那不是一封情书。

sentences.en: It was an instruction manual for life on Earth.
sentences.zh: 那是一份地球生活的使用说明书。

sentences.en: By June 2011, he was 47, and in home hospice.
sentences.zh: 到 2011 年 6 月，47 岁的他在家中接受临终关怀。

sentences.en: Seeger asked him how to get the roof rack that carried his canoes off the car.
sentences.zh: 西格问他如何把车顶上装独木舟的架子拆下来。

sentences.en: It's too complicated to explain,
sentences.zh: “解释起来太复杂了，”

sentences.en: Weverick said.
sentences.zh: 韦弗里克说。

sentences.en: That July, he died.
sentences.zh: 那年七月，他去世了。

sentences.en: The first couple of months after Weverick's death were weird.
sentences.zh: 韦弗里克去世后的头几个月很奇怪。

sentences.en: Seeger felt a surprising sense of relief from the uncertainties of sickness, a kind of liberation.
sentences.zh: 西格感到一种意想不到的解脱，摆脱了疾病带来的不确定性，这是一种解放。

sentences.en: She didn't care about conventions like money, which she had never needed to manage, and she took the boys on some epic trips.
sentences.zh: 她不在乎金钱之类的世俗观念，因为她从未需要操心这些，她带着孩子们进行了一些史诗般的旅行。

sentences.en: There are pictures of them smiling together in the deserts of New Mexico, on mountaintops in Hawaii.
sentences.zh: 照片里，他们在墨西哥新墨西哥州的沙漠中、在夏威夷的山顶上一起微笑着。

sentences.en: Then one day, she went into Boston for a haircut, got turned around, and accidentally walked into a lawyer's office next to the salon.
sentences.zh: 后来有一天，她去波士顿理发，走错了路，无意中走进了理发店隔壁的一间律师事务所。

sentences.en: Seeger ended up talking to a woman inside.
sentences.zh: 西格最终和里面的一位女士交谈起来。

sentences.en: That woman was also a widow, and she told Seeger that there would be a moment, as inevitable as death itself, when her feelings of release would be replaced
sentences.zh: 那位女士也是一位寡妇，她告诉西格，会有那么一个时刻，就像死亡本身一样不可避免，届时她那种解脱感会被取代，

sentences.en: by the more lasting aimlessness of the loSt.
sentences.zh: 被一种更持久的、迷失者的漫无目的感所取代。

sentences.en: Seeger walked back outside, and just like that, the world came out from under her feet.
sentences.zh: 西格走回街上，就在那一刻，世界从她脚下崩塌了。

sentences.en: She fell into an impossible blackness.
sentences.zh: 她坠入了一片绝望的黑暗中。

sentences.en: Later that winter, she took the boys sledding at the big hill in Concord.
sentences.zh: 那年冬天晚些时候，她带着孩子们去康科德的一座大山上滑雪橇。

sentences.en: Two other women and their children were there.
sentences.zh: 另外两位女士和她们的孩子也在那里。

sentences.en: Seeger stared at them coldly.
sentences.zh: 西格冷冷地盯着她们。

sentences.en: They were smiling, and carefree with their perfect, blissful lives.
sentences.zh: 她们微笑着，过着完美、幸福的生活，无忧无虑。

sentences.en: Seeger felt ugly and ruined next to them.
sentences.zh: 西格在她们身边感到自己丑陋而破碎。

sentences.en: Then Alex, who was six at the time, had a meltdown.
sentences.zh: 这时，当时六岁的亚历克斯崩溃大哭。

sentences.en: He sprawled himself across the hill so that the other children couldn't go down it.
sentences.zh: 他横躺在山坡上，挡住了其他孩子滑下去的路。

sentences.en: The two other mothers tried to get him to move.
sentences.zh: 另外两位母亲试图让他挪开。

sentences.en: He has a problem,
sentences.zh: “他有问题，”

sentences.en: Seeger told them.
sentences.zh: 西格对她们说。

sentences.en: They continued to try to shift him.
sentences.zh: 她们继续试图挪动他。

sentences.en: He has a problem,
sentences.zh: “他有问题，”

sentences.en: Seeger said.
sentences.zh: 西格说。

sentences.en: My husband died.
sentences.zh: “我丈夫去世了。”

sentences.en: Mine too, one of the other women said.
sentences.zh: “我的也是，”其中一位女士说。

sentences.en: That was Melissa.
sentences.zh: 那是梅丽莎。

sentences.en: A few weeks later, on Valentine's Day,
sentences.zh: 几周后的情人节，

sentences.en: Seeger was invited to her first gathering of the widows.
sentences.zh: 西格受邀参加了她的第一次寡妇聚会。

sentences.en: Today,
sentences.zh: 今天，

sentences.en: Melissa says she could detect the telltale flintiness of the recently bereaved the moment she saw Seeger on the hill.
sentences.zh: 梅丽莎说，她在山坡上看到西格的那一刻，就察觉到了新近丧偶者特有的那种坚硬。

sentences.en: Now there were six widows united in Concord, each middle-aged, each in a different stage of grief, drawn together by the peculiar pull of the unlucky.
sentences.zh: 现在，康科德有六位寡妇聚在一起，她们都已步入中年，处于不同的哀恸阶段，被不幸者之间那种奇特的吸引力联系在一起。

sentences.en: Three had been widowed by cancer, two by accidents, bicycling and hiking, and one by suicide.
sentences.zh: 其中三人因癌症丧偶，两人因事故（骑行和徒步），一人因自杀。

sentences.en: Melissa's husband was four years gone,
sentences.zh: 梅丽莎的丈夫去世四年了，

sentences.en: Seeger's seven months.
sentences.zh: 西格的丈夫去世七个月了。

sentences.en: Widowhood was like a new universe for Seeger to explore.
sentences.zh: 对于西格来说，守寡就像是一个有待探索的新宇宙。

sentences.en: She had never understood many social norMs.
sentences.zh: 她从未理解过许多社会规范。

sentences.en: The celebration of birthdays, for instance.
sentences.zh: 比如庆祝生日。

sentences.en: I just don't see the point, she says.
sentences.zh: “我就是不明白意义何在，”她说。

sentences.en: Why would I want to celebrate my birthday?
sentences.zh: “我为什么要庆祝自己的生日？”

sentences.en: Why on earth would I even care?
sentences.zh: “我到底为什么要关心这个？”

sentences.en: She had also drawn a hard line against Christmas and its myths.
sentences.zh: 她还对圣诞节及其神话划定了严格的界限。

sentences.en: I never wanted my kids to believe in Santa.
sentences.zh: “我从不希望我的孩子们相信圣诞老人。”

sentences.en: After Weverick's death, she became even more of a satellite, developing a deeper intolerance for life's ordinary concerns.
sentences.zh: 韦弗里克去世后，她变得更加像一颗卫星，对生活中普通的琐事愈发难以容忍。

sentences.en: Making dinner seemed an insurmountable chore, the routine of school lunches a form of torture.
sentences.zh: 做晚饭似乎是一项无法逾越的苦差事，准备学校午餐的日常简直是一种折磨。

sentences.en: The roof needed to be replaced, and she didn't have the faintest idea how to get it fixed.
sentences.zh: 屋顶需要更换，她根本不知道该怎么找人修理。

sentences.en: She wasn't sure how to swipe credit cards.
sentences.zh: 她甚至不确定怎么刷信用卡。

sentences.en: If the answers to her questions weren't somewhere on Weverick's three wrinkled sheets of paper, it could feel as though they were locked in a safe.
sentences.zh: 如果问题的答案不在韦弗里克那三张皱巴巴的纸上，她就会觉得答案被锁在了保险柜里。

sentences.en: There was a pendant light in her front hall where the boys would fight with their toy lightsabers, and sometimes they would hit the light with their wild swings.
sentences.zh: 门厅里有一盏吊灯，孩子们常在那里挥舞玩具光剑打闹，有时会击中那盏灯。

sentences.en: Seeger decided that either the light or one of the boys was going to end up damaged.
sentences.zh: 西格断定，要么是灯，要么是孩子们中的一个，迟早会受伤。

sentences.en: She asked the widows how to do electrical work.
sentences.zh: 她向那些寡妇请教如何进行电气维修。

sentences.en: I have to parcel out things with logic and evidence, she says.
sentences.zh: “我必须用逻辑和证据来处理事情，”她说。

sentences.en: Got out the ladder and took down the light, carefully wrapping black tape around the ends of the bare wires that now poked through the hole in the ceiling.
sentences.zh: 她拿出梯子取下灯，小心翼翼地用黑胶带缠住现在从天花板孔洞中露出的裸露电线末端。

sentences.en: She remembers thinking that her removing that light, all by herself, represented the height of her new accomplishment.
sentences.zh: 她记得当时想，自己独自一人拆掉那盏灯，代表了她新成就的巅峰。

sentences.en: She felt so reduced.
sentences.zh: 她感到自己如此渺小。

sentences.en: She felt so gigantic.
sentences.zh: 她又感到自己如此巨大。

sentences.en: For all of her real and perceived strangeness, the most unusual thing about Seeger is her blindness to her greatest gift.
sentences.zh: 尽管她有着种种真实或被认为的怪异之处，但西格最不寻常的地方在于她对自己最大天赋的视而不见。

sentences.en: She is more than aware of her preternatural mathematical abilities, her possession of a rare mind that can see numbers and their functions as clearly as the rest of us
sentences.zh: 她非常清楚自己超自然的数学能力，她拥有一个罕见的大脑，能像我们其他人看颜色和形状一样，

sentences.en: see colors and shapes.
sentences.zh: 清晰地看到数字及其函数。

sentences.en: I'm good at that stuff, she says with her brand of factual certainty that is sometimes confused with arrogance.
sentences.zh: “我擅长这些，”她以一种常被误认为是傲慢的事实确定性说道。

sentences.en: She knows she is unusually capable of turning abstract concepts into things that can be packed into a case.
sentences.zh: 她知道自己有非凡的能力，能将抽象概念转化为可以装进箱子的实物。

sentences.en: What she doesn't always see is her knack for connection between places, if not always people, the unconventional grace she possesses when it comes to closing
sentences.zh: 她不总是能看到的是，她在连接空间——如果不是人际关系的话——方面的天赋，以及她在跨越深不可测的距离时，

sentences.en: unfathomable distances.
sentences.zh: 所展现出的非凡优雅。

sentences.en: Seeger has lined the hallway outside her office with a series of magical travel posters put out by the Jet Propulsion Laboratory.
sentences.zh: 西格在办公室外的走廊里挂了一系列由喷气推进实验室发布的梦幻旅行海报。

sentences.en: Each gives a glimpse of the alien worlds that, in part, because of her, we now know exiSt.
sentences.zh: 每一张海报都让人得以一窥那些外星世界，而我们现在知道它们的存在，部分原因要归功于她。

sentences.en: There's a poster for Kepler-16b, an exoplanet that orbits a pair of stars, like Luke Skywalker's home planet of Tatooine.
sentences.zh: 有一张是关于开普勒-16b 的海报，这是一颗绕着一对恒星运行的系外行星，就像卢克·天行者的家乡塔图因星球一样。

sentences.en: Kepler-186f is depicted with red grass and red leaves on its trees because its star is cooler and redder than the sun, which might influence photosynthesis
sentences.zh: 开普勒-186f 被描绘成拥有红色的草地和红色的树叶，因为它的恒星比太阳更冷、更红，这可能会以改变叶片的方式影响光合作用。

sentences.en: in foliage-altering ways.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有一张关于 PSO J318.5-22 的海报，

sentences.en: There's even one for PSO
sentences.zh: 那是一颗流浪行星，它不绕恒星运行，而是在银河系中游荡，终年处于黑暗之中，沐浴在熔铁雨中。

sentences.en: J318.5-22, a rogue planet that doesn't orbit a star but instead wanders across the galaxy, cast in perpetual darkness, swept by rain of molten iron.
sentences.zh: 在发现比邻星 b 之后，

sentences.en: After the discovery of Proxima Centauri b,
sentences.zh: 西格为 Quartz 网站写了一张来自那里的银河明信片。

sentences.en: Seeger wrote a galactic postcard from it for the website Quartz.
sentences.zh: 她闭上眼睛，想象着一个远在 25 万亿英里之外的世界。

sentences.en: She closed her eyes and imagined a world
sentences.zh: 她写道，对于普通的地球人来说，访问这颗行星可能没什么乐趣。

sentences.en: 25 trillion miles away.
sentences.zh: 她看到一颗比地球大三分之一左右的行星，公转周期仅为 11 天。

sentences.en: For the average Earthling, she wrote, visiting this planet might not be much fun.
sentences.zh: 鉴于它靠近那颗微小的红矮星，她推测比邻星 b 上的紫外线辐射可能很强烈，但光线却像火星一样昏暗。

sentences.en: She saw a planet perhaps a third larger than Earth with an orbit of only 11 days.
sentences.zh: 她还推断出比邻星 b 是潮汐锁定的。

sentences.en: Given its proximity to its small, red star, she suggested that the ultraviolet radiation on Proxima Centauri b is probably intense, but the light,
sentences.zh: 光线，

sentences.en: Martian dim.
sentences.zh: 火星般昏暗。

sentences.en: She also deduced that Proxima Centauri b is tidally locked.
sentences.zh: 她还推断出比邻星 b 是潮汐锁定的。

sentences.en: Like the moon's relationship to Earth, one side of the planet always faces its star, which is always in the same place in its sky.
sentences.zh: 就像月球与地球的关系一样，行星的一面总是对着它的恒星，而恒星在它的天空中总是处于同一个位置。

sentences.en: Parts of Proxima Centauri b are cast in perpetual sunrise or sunset.
sentences.zh: 比邻星b的部分区域处于永恒的日出或日落之中。

sentences.en: One side is always in darkness.
sentences.zh: 另一面则永远处于黑暗之中。

sentences.en: At first, after Weverick's death,
sentences.zh: 起初，在Weverick去世后，

sentences.en: Seeger thought about abandoning her work because she was having such a hard time with her responsibilities at home.
sentences.zh: Seeger曾想过放弃她的工作，因为她在家里的责任让她感到非常吃力。

sentences.en: Her dean talked her out of quitting, giving her financial support to hire caregivers for the boys and urging her to redouble her efforts.
sentences.zh: 她的院长劝她不要辞职，并为她提供经济支持，让她雇人照顾孩子们，还敦促她加倍努力。

sentences.en: I had worked so hard, she says.
sentences.zh: “我曾经工作得那么努力，”她说。

sentences.en: I had all the years I called the lost years with Mike when I ignored him.
sentences.zh: “我和Mike在一起的那些年，我称之为失去的岁月，因为我忽略了他。”

sentences.en: We had little tiny kids.
sentences.zh: “我们当时有很小的孩子。”

sentences.en: I was working all the time, exhausted all the time.
sentences.zh: “我一直在工作，一直精疲力竭。”

sentences.en: But I was like, we'll have money someday.
sentences.zh: “但我当时想，总有一天我们会赚到钱的。”

sentences.en: We'll have time someday.
sentences.zh: “总有一天我们会拥有时间的。”

sentences.en: She paused.
sentences.zh: 她停顿了一下。

sentences.en: Her face was blank, emotionless.
sentences.zh: 她的脸面无表情，没有流露任何情绪。

sentences.en: Now I'll cry.
sentences.zh: “现在我要哭了。”

sentences.en: Seconds later, tears spilled out of her eyes and her voice modulated.
sentences.zh: 几秒钟后，泪水从她眼中夺眶而出，她的声音也随之颤抖。

sentences.en: I wanted to make it up to him.
sentences.zh: “我本想补偿他的。”

sentences.en: And I never did.
sentences.zh: “但我从未做到。”

sentences.en: Seeger has always found comfort and perhaps even solace in her work, in her search for another and maybe better version of our world.
sentences.zh: Seeger总能在工作中找到慰藉，甚至可能是安抚，在寻找另一个、也许是更好的世界版本的过程中找到慰藉。

sentences.en: In her mourning, each discovery represented one more avenue of escape.
sentences.zh: 在她哀悼的日子里，每一个发现都代表着多一条逃避的途径。

sentences.en: In the spring of 2013, she was given responsibility for the starshade.
sentences.zh: 2013年春天，她被委以“星影”（starshade）项目的重任。

sentences.en: That July, she met a tall, fast-walking man named Charles Darrow.
sentences.zh: 那年七月，她遇见了一位身材高大、走路很快的男人，名叫Charles Darrow。

sentences.en: Darrow, who is now 53, was an amateur astronomer and the president of the Toronto branch of the Royal Astronomical
sentences.zh: 现年53岁的Darrow是一位业余天文学家，也是加拿大皇家天文学会

sentences.en: Society of Canada.
sentences.zh: 多伦多分会的会长。

sentences.en: And at the last minute, he decided to go to the society's annual meeting in Thunder Bay, Ontario.
sentences.zh: 在最后一刻，他决定去参加在安大略省桑德贝举行的学会年会。

sentences.en: Darrow was on his way out of a profoundly unhappy marriage.
sentences.zh: Darrow当时正处于一段极度不幸的婚姻中，正准备从中解脱。

sentences.en: He worked for his family business, an engine parts wholesaler.
sentences.zh: 他在家族企业工作，那是一家汽车零部件批发商。

sentences.en: He needed a break, and he pointed his car north.
sentences.zh: 他需要休息一下，于是他开车向北驶去。

sentences.en: I wanted to be alone, he says.
sentences.zh: “我想一个人待着，”他说。

sentences.en: At a reception on the Friday evening,
sentences.zh: 在周五晚上的招待会上，

sentences.en: Darrow noticed a hazel-eyed woman staring at him from across the room.
sentences.zh: Darrow注意到一位有着淡褐色眼睛的女人正从房间对面盯着他看。

sentences.en: I thought she was looking at someone behind me, he says.
sentences.zh: “我以为她在看我身后的人，”他说。

sentences.en: Then he went into the lecture hall, and the same woman was that night's keynote speaker.
sentences.zh: 后来他走进报告厅，发现当晚的主讲人正是那位女士。

sentences.en: She talked about exoplanets.
sentences.zh: 她谈论的是系外行星。

sentences.en: The next day, lunch was in a university cafeteria.
sentences.zh: 第二天，午餐是在大学食堂吃的。

sentences.en: The woman was in the salad line ahead of him, and she turned around.
sentences.zh: 那位女士排在他前面的沙拉队里，她转过身来。

sentences.en: Darrow mustered up his courage and invited Sarah Seeger to join him.
sentences.zh: Darrow鼓起勇气，邀请Sarah Seeger和他一起坐。

sentences.en: I knew about five minutes into the conversation that my life was going to change, he says.
sentences.zh: “谈话进行了大约五分钟，我就知道我的人生要改变了，”他说。

sentences.en: Seeger was taken with Darrow the night she saw him in Thunder Bay.
sentences.zh: Seeger在桑德贝见到Darrow的那晚就被他吸引了。

sentences.en: She had been struck by the contrast between the whiteness of his shirt and his tanned summer skin.
sentences.zh: 他衬衫的洁白与他晒成古铜色的夏日肤色之间的反差让她印象深刻。

sentences.en: But she didn't have the same certainty that possessed him at their lunch the next day.
sentences.zh: 但她并没有像他第二天午餐时那样拥有同样的确定性。

sentences.en: She wasn't sure how to develop a relationship across the 549 miles between her home in Concord and his home outside Toronto.
sentences.zh: 她不确定如何跨越她位于康科德的家和他在多伦多郊外的家之间那549英里的距离来发展一段关系。

sentences.en: She thought they might never cross paths again.
sentences.zh: 她以为他们可能再也不会有交集了。

sentences.en: They might not have, except Darrow resolved during his drive back home that he had to call her.
sentences.zh: 他们可能确实不会再有交集，除非Darrow在开车回家的路上决定他必须给她打电话。

sentences.en: He picked up the phone five times but always hung up before she answered.
sentences.zh: 他拿起电话拨了五次，但每次都在她接听前挂断了。

sentences.en: On the 6th, he spoke to her, beginning a long correspondence, emails and conversations over Skype.
sentences.zh: 到了第6天，他终于和她通了话，开启了一段漫长的通信，通过电子邮件和Skype进行交流。

sentences.en: Darrow and Seeger talked every way but face to face.
sentences.zh: Darrow和Seeger以各种方式交谈，唯独没有面对面。

sentences.en: They fell in love remotely.
sentences.zh: 他们远程坠入了爱河。

sentences.en: I had to follow my heart,
sentences.zh: “我必须追随我的内心，”

sentences.en: Darrow says.
sentences.zh: Darrow说。

sentences.en: I decided that I wasn't going to die unhappy.
sentences.zh: “我决定我不能带着遗憾死去。”

sentences.en: Melissa, meanwhile, told Seeger that if she could close the gap between here and a planet like Kepler-186f, a journey that would take us 500 light years to complete,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，Melissa告诉Seeger，如果她能缩短这里与像开普勒-186f这样的行星之间的距离——那是一段需要我们走500光年的旅程——

sentences.en: then the 549 miles between Concord and Toronto shouldn't seem like such an insurmountable gulf.
sentences.zh: 那么康科德和多伦多之间的549英里就不应该看起来像是无法逾越的鸿沟。

sentences.en: By her usual measures, he was right next door.
sentences.zh: 按照她通常的衡量标准，他就在隔壁。

sentences.en: Seeger and Darrow married in April 2015.
sentences.zh: Seeger和Darrow于2015年4月结婚。

sentences.en: In different ways, each had rescued the other.
sentences.zh: 以不同的方式，他们各自拯救了对方。

sentences.en: Seeger was the cataclysm that allowed Darrow to make every correction.
sentences.zh: Seeger是那场让Darrow做出彻底改变的剧变。

sentences.en: He divorced, left his family business, and moved into a pretty yellow
sentences.zh: 他离婚了，离开了家族企业，搬进了一栋漂亮的黄色

sentences.en: Victorian in Concord.
sentences.zh: 维多利亚式住宅，位于康科德。

sentences.en: The two boys started calling him dad.
sentences.zh: 两个男孩开始叫他爸爸。

sentences.en: For Seeger,
sentences.zh: 对于Seeger来说，

sentences.en: Darrow was a second chance to know love, even deeper than the one she had known because it seemed so improbable in her sadness.
sentences.zh: Darrow是第二次了解爱的机会，甚至比她以前所知的爱更深，因为在她的悲伤中，这似乎太不可思议了。

sentences.en: I feel so lucky to have found him,
sentences.zh: “能找到他，我感到非常幸运，”

sentences.en: Seeger says.
sentences.zh: Seeger说。

sentences.en: What are the chances?
sentences.zh: “几率有多大呢？”

sentences.en: Adapting to his new life hasn't always been easy for Darrow.
sentences.zh: 对于Darrow来说，适应他的新生活并不总是那么容易。

sentences.en: He is determined, as he puts it, to make Sarah the happiest woman in the multiverse.
sentences.zh: 正如他所说，他决心让Sarah成为多元宇宙中最幸福的女人。

sentences.en: He cooks dinner.
sentences.zh: 他做晚饭。

sentences.en: He helps take care of the boys.
sentences.zh: 他帮忙照顾孩子们。

sentences.en: He maintains the house.
sentences.zh: 他打理房子。

sentences.en: He walks with Seeger to the train station every morning, and he picks her up every night.
sentences.zh: 他每天早上陪Seeger走到火车站，每天晚上去接她。

sentences.en: He has chosen to take care of the mundane so that she can devote herself to the extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 他选择处理琐事，这样她就可以全身心投入到非凡的事业中。

sentences.en: But he banged his head more than once on Weverick's canoe, which still hung from the back of the garage.
sentences.zh: 但他不止一次撞到Weverick的独木舟上，那独木舟仍然挂在车库后面。

sentences.en: Not long ago,
sentences.zh: 不久前，

sentences.en: Darrow was looking for the right ways to assert his presence, to make a claim to a house that didn't always feel like his.
sentences.zh: Darrow一直在寻找合适的方式来彰显他的存在，对一个并不总是让他感到归属的家宣示主权。

sentences.en: The wires dangling from the front hall ceiling bothered him.
sentences.zh: 前厅天花板上垂下的电线让他很烦恼。

sentences.en: They looked bad and seemed dangerous.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来很糟糕，而且似乎很危险。

sentences.en: A few months after his arrival in Concord, he took his opening.
sentences.zh: 在他搬到康科德几个月后，他抓住了机会。

sentences.en: He carved out some of the plaster, installed a plastic box, ran the wires through it, and hooked up a new fixture, flush-mounted, so that the boys wouldn't hit it
sentences.zh: 他凿开了一些灰泥，安装了一个塑料盒，把电线穿过盒子，并接上了一个新的嵌入式灯具，这样孩子们就不会在

sentences.en: during their duels.
sentences.zh: 决斗时撞到它。

sentences.en: Darrow climbed down from the ladder and flicked the switch.
sentences.zh: Darrow从梯子上下来，按下了开关。

sentences.en: The morning after she forgot her phone,
sentences.zh: 在Seeger忘记带手机的第二天早上，

sentences.en: Seeger woke up and decided, just like that, to skip the commute.
sentences.zh: Seeger醒来后决定，就这样，不去上班了。

sentences.en: With the house to herself, she tried to make coffee.
sentences.zh: 独自在家，她试着煮咖啡。

sentences.en: She left out part of the machine, and after some terrible noises, the pot was bone dry.
sentences.zh: 她漏装了机器的一部分，在一阵可怕的噪音过后，咖啡壶里干得一滴不剩。

sentences.en: She sat down at her kitchen table with her empty mug and began talking about hundreds of billions of galaxies and their hundreds of billions of stars.
sentences.zh: 她坐在餐桌旁，拿着空杯子，开始谈论数千亿个星系和它们数千亿颗恒星。

sentences.en: Tens of billions of habitable planets, far more of them than there are people on Earth.
sentences.zh: 数百亿颗宜居行星，它们的数量远多于地球上的人口。

sentences.en: There has to be other life somewhere out there.
sentences.zh: 在某个地方一定有其他生命存在。

sentences.en: We can't be that special.
sentences.zh: 我们不可能那么特别。

sentences.en: It would be arrogant to think so,
sentences.zh: “那样想太傲慢了，”

sentences.en: Seeger said.
sentences.zh: Seeger说。

sentences.en: But in her lifetime, after the WFIRST telescope rockets into orbit, and maybe her starshade follows it, she puts the chances of success at 85%.
sentences.zh: 但在她有生之年，在WFIRST望远镜发射升空，也许她的“星影”紧随其后之后，她认为成功的几率是85%。

sentences.en: She will have time to explore only the nearest hundred stars or so.
sentences.zh: 她将只有时间去探索最近的一百颗左右的恒星。

sentences.en: A hundred stars out of all those lights in the sky.
sentences.zh: 天空中所有那些光点中的一百颗恒星。

sentences.en: A fraction of a fraction of a fraction
sentences.zh: 在这一小部分中的一小部分中的一小部分里，

sentences.en: will one of them have a small, rocky planet like Earth?
sentences.zh: 其中一颗会有像地球一样的小型岩石行星吗？

sentences.en: Probably.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: Will one of those small, rocky planets have liquid water on it?
sentences.zh: 这些小型岩石行星中会有一颗上面有液态水吗？

sentences.en: Possibly.
sentences.zh: 有可能。

sentences.en: Will the planet sustain life?
sentences.zh: 这颗行星会维持生命吗？

sentences.en: Now the odds tilt.
sentences.zh: 现在几率开始倾斜了。

sentences.en: Now they are working against her, and she knows it.
sentences.zh: 现在它们对她不利，她很清楚这一点。

sentences.en: Now there may be one in a million that she'll find what she's looking for.
sentences.zh: 现在可能要百万分之一的几率，她才能找到她正在寻找的东西。

sentences.en: She did some private math.
sentences.zh: 她私下做了一些计算。

sentences.en: I believe, she said.
sentences.zh: “我相信，”她说。

sentences.en: Seeger's discovery will be fate-altering if it comes.
sentences.zh: 如果Seeger的发现真的到来，那将是改变命运的时刻。

sentences.en: But it will also be quiet.
sentences.zh: 但它也会是安静的。

sentences.en: A few pixels on a screen.
sentences.zh: 屏幕上的几个像素点。

sentences.en: It will obey the laws of physics.
sentences.zh: 它将遵循物理定律。

sentences.en: It will be a probability equation.
sentences.zh: 它将是一个概率方程。

sentences.en: What are the chances?
sentences.zh: 几率有多大？

sentences.en: We won't discover that there is life on other planets the way we've been taught that we'll learn.
sentences.zh: 我们发现其他行星上有生命的方式，不会是我们被教导的那样。

sentences.en: There won't be some great mothership descending from the sky over Johannesburg, or a bizarre lightning storm that monsters will ride to New Jersey.
sentences.zh: 不会有什么巨大的母舰降临在约翰内斯堡上空，也不会有什么怪物骑着离奇的闪电风暴来到新泽西。

sentences.en: What Seeger will have is a photograph from a space telescope of a distant solar system, with its star eclipsed by her starshade, and with a familiar blue dot some safe
sentences.zh: Seeger将拥有的是一张来自太空望远镜的遥远太阳系的照片，它的恒星被她的“星影”遮挡，而在一个安全

sentences.en: and survivable distance away from it.
sentences.zh: 且可生存的距离外，有一个熟悉的蓝色小点。

sentences.en: That's all the evidence she will have that we're not alone, and that will be all the evidence she will need.
sentences.zh: 这就是她证明我们并不孤单的全部证据，而这也将是她所需要的全部证据。

sentences.en: Her proof of life will be a small light where there wasn't one before.
sentences.zh: 她证明生命存在的证据，将是一个以前不存在的小光点。
